subject: BlueCrest renewal + capacity uplift — staged price shelter counterproposal
messages:
From: Anna Liu <anna@bluecrest.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bluecrest.com
Date: 2028-08-25T14:02:00Z
Subject: Renewal questions + ask on price shelter and credits

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the renewal reminder — we’ve been reviewing usage and expect to bump our committed capacity from ~2M tokens/month to ~5M tokens/month for 2029. Before we proceed, procurement has two asks: a 6‑month price shelter (to lock current rate while we ramp) and a one‑time operational credit to offset integration testing costs.

Can Redwood accommodate a 25% discount on committed tier pricing for the first 3 months of the term plus a $30k credit? If that’s not possible, we’d like to see alternative structures (phased discounts, short price holds, or invoice timing changes). We’re fast approaching our renewal window and need to include this in our board materials.

Appreciate any flexibility — happy to jump on a call this week.

Best,
Anna Liu
Head of Platform Partnerships
BlueCrest Analytics

--
Attachment: BlueCrest_Renewal_Request.xlsx (spreadsheet of projected usage)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna@bluecrest.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-25T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal questions + ask on price shelter and credits

Hi Anna — thanks for the clarity and the projection. Congrats on the planned uplift. I’ve looped in Ben (sales lead) to work through economics and Markus to confirm legal/appetite for a short shelter. I’ll propose a couple options by EOD tomorrow.

Quick note on constraints: longer price shelters and large upfront credits are tricky for our margin profile, but we usually can do staged concessions tied to commit and billing cadence.

Talk soon,
Rachel
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-26T09:07:00Z
Subject: Fwd: BlueCrest renewal asks — need concession plan and legal guardrails

Folks — forwarding BlueCrest’s request. Key points:
- Commit uplift: 2M -> 5M tokens/month (start of term)
- Customer asks: 6‑month price shelter at current rate + $30k one‑time credit
- They’re open to alternatives: phased discounts or invoice timing adjustments

What I need: a concise counter (no more than two options) that preserves margin but gives the customer runway. Prefer a staged approach tied to commit milestones or a smaller initial credit plus ramped discounts. Also flag any legal or billing blockers for a 6‑month price shelter.

Thanks — Rachel

> 
> Thanks for the renewal reminder — we’ve been reviewing usage and expect to bump our committed capacity...

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-01T11:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Fwd: BlueCrest renewal asks — need concession plan and legal guardrails

Thanks for the context. My proposed commercial counter (two options):

Option A — Accelerated commit + small credit (preferred):
- Commit: 5M tokens/month (annual term)
- Price: 12% discount to list on first 3 months, then 6% thereafter (tiered by usage if below committed level we apply short true‑up mechanics)
- One‑time operational credit: $15,000 applied to first invoice (to offset integration/test costs)
- Price shelter: 3‑month guaranteed rate on the discounted price (we can commit to that in MAA)
- Net impact to Redwood: limited and tied to ramp; preserves our long‑term revenue when they stay at commit.

Option B — Longer shelter, smaller credit (if they insist):
- Commit: 5M tokens/month
- Price: 10% discount baseline, with a 6‑month price shelter at that level
- One‑time operational credit: $8,000
- Requires finance approval for revenue recognition treatment and a short amortization schedule for the credit.

We shouldn’t do the full 25% requested — it’s outside our allowable concession band for this tier. If they push, we can trade some non‑monetary items (extended onboarding hours, priority review in Optimize) rather than deeper discounts.

Markus — can you confirm whether Option A’s 3‑month shelter is OK operationally and whether legal needs specific language around phased rollback? Monica — if finance needs to sign off on the credit timing, flag now.

— Ben

--
Attachment: none

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-03T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: BlueCrest renewal asks — need concession plan and legal guardrails

Ben — Option A is acceptable from legal/commercial risk perspective. A few notes:
- 3‑month price shelter is fine; we should include explicit language that ties the shelter to the signed MAA and commit. If consumption falls >40% below committed, we reserve right to reprice after a 30‑day notice.
- The $15k credit should be treated as a one‑time billing credit (not a discount applied to unit price) and documented in the amendment; finance needs to record for revenue ops.
- Add a clause that the staged discount schedule is contingent on hitting commit milestones at months 1 and 4.

Monica — please confirm finance treatment and that we can apply the $15k to first invoice without delaying recognition. If not, suggest amortizing across first two invoices.

Markus
Chief Commercial Counsel

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna@bluecrest.com>, procurement@bluecrest.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-18T10:12:00Z
Subject: BlueCrest renewal — counterproposal and next steps

Hi Anna — thanks for the patience while we dug into internal constraints. We want to make this renewal simple and predictable as you scale. Attached is our formal counter (Redwood_Renewal_Counter_BC-2028-RNW-003.pdf) and a short MAA amendment (MAA_v2.docx) capturing the shelter and credit mechanics. High level: 

1) Preferred commercial path (Option A) — faster ramp, modest credit
- Commit: 5M tokens/month, 12% discount applied to list pricing for months 1–3, reverting to 6% thereafter for the term.
- One‑time operational credit: $15,000 applied to first invoice.
- Price shelter: 3‑month guaranteed rate on the discounted price, contingent on signed amendment and meeting initial usage checkpoint (month 1).
- Milestone language: if consumption drops >40% vs commit within month 1, we’ll engage on a short true‑up rather than automatic reprovisioning.

2) Alternate (Option B) — if BlueCrest requires a longer guarantee: 10% baseline discount + 6‑month shelter + $8k credit.

If either option is acceptable, I can initiate DocuSign (link included) and loop in billing to align invoice date to your fiscal cadence. If you prefer, we can swap part of the credit for 20 hours of prioritized onboarding and an Optimize cost review session.

Next steps: pick Option A or B, and confirm the signatory for the MAA. I’ll open the DocuSign envelope once you confirm and push finance/billing on our side to prepare the first invoice with the credit applied.

Appreciate the partnership — excited to support BlueCrest’s growth.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
